preamble: The Middle Chinese voiced alveolo-palatal affricate [dʑ] of the 常/禪 initial (Baxter dzy-) became the Mandarin fricative [ʂ] in oblique-tone (rising, departing, entering) syllables, and in some level-tone words such as 時 shí; other level-tone words have aspirated [ʈʂʰ] (常 cháng, 成 chéng). This follows the modern reconstruction of Pulleyblank, Baxter and Zhengzhang Shangfang, in which 禪 is [dʑ] and 船 is the fricative [ʑ]; the Song rime tables, followed by Karlgren, had the two values reversed.
sources: Pulleyblank, E. G. (1984). Middle Chinese: A Study in Historical Phonology. UBC Press. https://www.ubcpress.ca/middle-chinese
